raw_segments.text: The same quantity of silver, it may perhaps be said, will, in the present times, even
according to the account which has been here given, purchase a much smaller quantity of
several sorts of provisions than it would have done during some part of the last century.
And to ascertain whether this change be owing to a rise in the value of those goods, or
to a fall in the value of silver, is only to establish a vain and useless distinction,
which can be of no sort of service to the man who has only a certain quantity of silver
to go to market with, or a certain fixed revenue in money.

It may not, however, upon that account be altogether useless.
